newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Democrats campaign ahead of Tuesday primary.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Democrats campaign ahead of Tuesday primary.

text.p: New Jersey Democrats head to the polls Tuesday to decide whether U.S. Rep. Rob Andrews, state Senator Jim McGreevey or former Morris County Prosecutor Michael Murphy should be the party's standard bearer in November against Governor Christine Whitman.
The three men spent much of the weekend appealing to an important part of their party's base -- black and Hispanic voters in the inner cities.

Andrews held a rally in Camden on Saturday while McGreevey and Murphy appeared at a forum at the Abyssinia Baptist Church in Newark. McGreevey remained in New Jersey Sunday to visit black churches during morning services while his rivals appeared on a New York television show.

All are relatively young, and all have considerable government experience. Andrews and McGreevey are elected officials, while Murphy was home-schooled in politics as the stepson of former Governor Richard Hughes. He also served several years as Morris County prosecutor.
Both Andrews and McGreevey have tried to position themselves as fiscal conservatives, and both have backing from county committees and the state's Democratic elite.

Murphy advocates a 25-cent increase in the cigarette tax to fund state aid for public schools. He entered the campaign with support from some of his father's old friends and billed himself as the "un-candidate."
Murphy has also won the endorsement of newspapers including the Philadelphia Inquirer and the Trenton Times.
